name: ANAD Eating Disorders Helpline
summary: Support and resources for individuals struggling with eating disorders and their loved ones.

sections.title: About ANAD
sections.text: The National Association of Anorexia Nervosa and Associated Disorders (ANAD) is one of the oldest nonprofit organizations dedicated to eating disorder awareness, prevention, and recovery support. Founded in 1976, ANAD provides free peer support services, educational resources, and advocacy for individuals affected by eating disorders and their families. ANAD believes that recovery is possible and works to provide hope and support to those on the journey to healing.

sections.title: ANAD Helpline
sections.text: ANAD's Helpline at 1-888-375-7767 provides free support, information, and referrals for anyone affected by an eating disorder. Helpline staff can help you understand eating disorders, find treatment providers, locate support groups, and navigate recovery challenges. The helpline serves individuals with eating disorders, concerned family members and friends, and professionals seeking resources. Staff provide compassionate, non-judgmental support and can help you take the next step toward recovery.

sections.title: Free Support Groups
sections.text: ANAD operates free support groups for individuals in recovery from eating disorders and for their loved ones. Support groups meet virtually, making them accessible from anywhere. Groups are led by trained facilitators who have personal experience with eating disorder recovery. In these groups, members share their experiences, struggles, and victories in a confidential, supportive environment. Specialized groups are available for different stages of recovery and for specific populations including teens, men, and parents.

sections.title: Understanding Eating Disorders
sections.text: ANAD provides education about all types of eating disorders including anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, ARFID, and other specified feeding and eating disorders. Educational resources cover warning signs, health consequences, treatment options, and recovery processes. ANAD emphasizes that eating disorders are serious mental illnesses that affect people of all genders, ages, races, and body sizes. Early intervention improves outcomes, and recovery is possible at any stage.

sections.title: Recovery Resources
sections.text: Beyond the helpline and support groups, ANAD offers a treatment directory to help individuals and families find eating disorder specialists. The website provides recovery tools, meal support resources, and educational materials for various stages of the recovery journey. ANAD's Recovery Mentorship Program connects those in recovery with mentors who have successfully navigated their own recovery. The organization also provides resources for educators, coaches, and healthcare providers on recognizing and responding to eating disorders.
